chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who had intercourse with his wife in the month of Ramadan and did not find what to give in charity to sixty poor people, he said: 'He gives in charity what he is able to.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a person who cannot afford to feed sixty poor people after breaking their Ramadan fast?
ai.summary: In the Shia jurisprudential tradition, this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of *kaffarah* (expiation) for *jam'* (sexual intercourse) during Ramadan, specifically addressing the middle tier of expiation: feeding sixty poor people. It establishes that for those unable to meet the full obligation, the requirement is scaled to their actual financial capacity (*ma yutiq*), reflecting the principle of *taysir* (ease) in divine law. This ruling is often discussed alongside the primary expiation of freeing a slave and the secondary option of fasting two consecutive months, highlighting the graduated nature of the penalty based on ability.
